the_signal.headline: SOC 2 automation now table stakes for enterprise GTM velocity
the_signal.body: n8n's SOC 2 compliance automation framework shows that evidence collection, monitoring, and remediation across heterogeneous stacks is no longer a sales blocker—it's a deployment prerequisite. GTM teams selling to enterprises need compliance automation baked into their workflow layer before deal close, not after. This shifts your go-to-market from 'we'll handle compliance later' to 'compliance is built-in infrastructure.'

tool_drop.name: Cloudways Managed AI Agents
tool_drop.what: Hosted AI agent orchestration with managed infrastructure for multi-agent workflows.
tool_drop.why: Removes operational overhead for GTM teams deploying agents at scale—you get observability and coordination without maintaining your own agent control plane.

thread_of_day.title: AGENTS.md feature request signals agent governance is becoming standardized
thread_of_day.takeaway: The community is pushing for standardized agent capability declarations—similar to how README.md works—which means agent discovery, permissions, and multi-agent coordination are moving from ad-hoc to declarative.

quote.text: RPA versus workflow automation—see how they stack up across reliability, security, scalability, observability, and long-term operations.

whats_moving.context: n8n's SOC 2 automation guides suggest enterprises now expect compliance evidence collection built into workflow platforms—not bolted on.
AGENTS.md feature request shows the community is converging on declarative agent specs, which will force GTM teams to document agent capabilities and permissions.
n8n alternatives comparison and Cloudways Managed AI Agents signal enterprises are moving away from vendor-locked SaaS agents toward deployable, governance-first platforms.

act_on_this: Audit your agent deployment process for SOC 2 readiness—specifically evidence collection and monitoring across your workflow stack—and document it as a pre-close deliverable, not a post-close burden.
